data.narrative:
X-Bow Systems, a Series B-stage defense and security company founded by Jason Hundley, Mark Kaufman, and Maureen Gannon, is evaluated against a peer set of 8 private companies and 2 public comparables in the Defense & Security sector.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the company's $157M total raised, implying a valuation of $298M. Peer-median analysis references 8 same-sector, same-stage private companies—including Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), and Twenty ($1.0B)—which generate a median valuation of $1.1B. The peer range spans $300M to $3.0B.

The two methods produce a wide dispersion, reflecting material uncertainty in how X-Bow Systems ranks within the Defense & Security Series B cohort. The triangulated analysis supports a range of $254M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $712M. The low end anchors to stage-progression mechanics; the high end reflects peer-median positioning. Key uncertainties include X-Bow's differentiation within the peer set, its revenue trajectory relative to comparables, and customer concentration in government or commercial segments. Further diligence on unit economics and contract pipeline would narrow the range.
